title: Prophylaxis of Retinal Breaks: Clinical Decision Matrix
summary: A comprehensive guide to identifying and managing peripheral retinal lesions. This poster delineates when to observe and when to intervene with laser photocoagulation or cryotherapy to prevent rhegmatogenous retinal detachment (RRD).

sections.title: Clinical Definition & Overview
sections.content: A retinal break is a full-thickness continuity defect in the neurosensory retina. Prophylaxis aims to create a chorioretinal adhesion around the break using laser photocoagulation or cryopexy, preventing liquefied vitreous from entering the subretinal space and causing a Rhegmatogenous Retinal Detachment (RRD). The decision to treat is a risk-benefit calculation based on symptoms, morphology, and systemic risk factors.

rows: Round plug of retina pulled off

sections.title: Treatment Indications: Symptomatic Lesions
content: Symptomatic Horseshoe Tears (HST): Mandatory treatment.
Symptomatic Dialysis: Mandatory treatment.
Symptomatic Operculated Tears: Treat if traction persists or large.
Symptomatic Lattice with Breaks: Treat holes/tears within lattice.
New Flashes/Floaters with Pigmented Cells (Shafer's Sign): Urgent intervention.

sections.title: Treatment Indications: Asymptomatic Lesions
content: HST in Fellow Eye of RD: Highly recommended.
Large Atrophic Holes in Myopes: Consider if >2DD.
Lattice Degeneration in Fellow Eye of RD: Strong consideration.
Subclinical RD (localized fluid >1DD): Usually treat.
Pre-Cataract/Refractive Surgery: Treat visible HST/high-risk lattice.

sections.title: Red Flags: Impending RD
content: Shafer's Sign (Tobacco Dust in anterior vitreous)
Vitreous Hemorrhage (70% risk of associated tear)
New onset 'curtain' or 'veil' in vision
Macular involving subretinal fluid

sections.title: Surgical Technique: Laser Photocoagulation
content: 1. Topical anesthesia and Goldmann 3-Mirror or wide-field lens.
2. Argon/532nm Green Laser: 200-500 micron spot size.
3. Exposure: 0.1 to 0.2 seconds.
4. Power: Titrate to obtain 'grey-white' uptake.
5. Pattern: 3 concentric rows of confluent burns around the break.
6. Extension: Ensure the 'horns' of the HST are well-surrounded.

sections.title: Cryopexy: When to Use?
content: Indications: Extreme periphery (Ora), hazy media (cataract/hemorrhage).
Mechanism: Freeze-thaw-freeze cycle to create adhesion.
Disadvantage: Increased risk of PVR due to RPE dispersion.
Procedure: Direct visualization with indirect ophthalmoscopy.

rows: Small risk of HST at posterior end
Asymptomatic lattice has very low progression to RD (~1%).
Symptomatic HST carry a 50% risk of RD without treatment.
Recommends against treating asymptomatic holes/lattice in low-risk eyes.
Fellow eyes of RD patients have a 10-15% cumulative risk of RD.

content.explanation: 3 rows of burns, 200-500 micron size, 1 (one) goal: prevent fluid entry.

sections.title: Complications of Prophylaxis
content: Epiretinal Membrane (ERM) formation (most common).
Iatrogenic retinal breaks.
Vitreous hemorrhage.
Subretinal neovascularization (rare).
Failure of prophylaxis: RD occurs despite laser.

sections.title: Clinical Pearls for the Exam
content: Always perform scleral depression to rule out additional breaks before lasering.
Pigmented breaks are 'old' and usually stable, but symptoms override pigmentation.
If you find one break, look 180 degrees away; multiple breaks are common.
Wait 10-14 days for the laser scar to achieve maximal tensile strength.
Educate patients on the 'RD Warning Signs' even after successful laser.
